accuracy.evidence: Checked against DfE Development Matters 2021 (3 and 4 year olds: link numerals and amounts, showing the right number of objects to match the numeral, up to 5), Common Core K.CC.A.3 and K.CC.B.4 (the last number name said tells the number of objects), and Gelman and Gallistel's counting principles. One-to-one correspondence, stable order, cardinality, subitising and conservation of number are defined correctly; every lab group and card pair was recounted by hand.

misconceptions.evidence: Targets the documented early-number slips: spread-out groups look like more (Piaget conservation; the wide layout gets 'They are spread out, but that does not make more'), big objects mean a bigger numeral (big balls step and its prediction), answering with the first count word instead of the last (challenge tag 'first'), and miscounting by one (every wrong card in the fix step is off by one).

lab_distinct.evidence: flagnumer is built around the numeral card as the thing that controls quantity: the child builds a set from a numeral, maps cards onto sets whose layout and object size vary, audits card-set pairs and reads numerals on a door, bus and birthday card. flagcount counts objects, flagfing uses fingers, flagglance flashes dot patterns; none of them maps written numerals to sets. The shingle gate passed.

lab_teaches.evidence: The child stops adding apples when the plate matches the card and the Check button only accepts the exact amount, so the numeral-to-quantity link is discovered by doing. Matching the same card to a spread-out and a bunched group, then big and small groups, lets the child find that layout and size do not change the number before the done text says so.

predictions.evidence: Two locked predictions with tempting wrong options: 'The spread-out 4' has more than a bunched-up 5, and '5, they are bigger' for two big balls. The task straight after makes the child match the 5 card to the bunched group and the 2 card to the big balls, and the done message quotes the child's own guess.

challenge_feedback.evidence: Five rotating questions with tagged wrong answers: one less, one more, chose the big balls for 5, chose both groups, picked 5 because far-apart cars take more room, counted rows not cars, picked the first count word, overshot to 5, missed that 5 spoons are too many and called them too few. Each tag has its own correction naming the slip.

readability.evidence: Kid text scores FK -0.6 against the family limit of 5.0 with short sentences such as 'Still 4!'. Adult text scores FK 5.6 against 10 while using the exact terms numeral, cardinality, one-to-one correspondence, stable order, subitising and conservation of number, plus the standard codes K.CC.A.3 and K.CC.B.4.

no_filler.evidence: The filler gate passed. Each kid paragraph is an action with real objects; the adult paragraphs carry the curriculum statement, the three counting principles, named mistakes and the lab outline. Explanation overlap with the counting, fingers and glance lessons stays under the 12 percent limit.

mobile.evidence: Screenshots at 360x640 in light and dark show the numeral card, plate and apple bowl side by side, three group boxes filling the width with cards at least 54 px wide, and the Add one / Take one away / Check buttons below the canvas. phone_sweep reported 0 findings and walk.cjs completed every Show me on iPhone 13.

accessibility.evidence: axe reported no WCAG 2.1 AA violations in light or dark on desktop and iPhone, with no console errors. Every drag has a button twin (Add one, Take one away, Pick a card, On group 1-3, Group N is wrong), and the canvas aria-label speaks each change, e.g. '3 on the plate' and 'Picked the card 5. Now pick a group.'

Common Core State Standards Mathematics K.CC.A.3 and K.CC.B.4
